rubric_notes: Complete: class a > a.22 > a.22.1 > families a.22.1.0-a.22.1.4 with evidence-backed members (NC2, NF-Y, Chrac, Sos, Aq_328, TTHA1479); superfamily supports shared ancestry not shared function; nucleosome/chromatin function explicitly not transferred; notes bacterial members are hypothetical proteins; H1/H5, modifying enzymes and j.63 fragment correctly excluded with 'not homologous in SCOPe' framing; release and pagination limits stated. 'Descend from a common ancestor' slightly stronger than 'probable' but acceptable. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Correct sccs, sunids, family/protein/species labels and superfamily-level conclusion with no closer claim; rejects transfer of HisE substrate, catalytic residues, cofactor, pathway and oligomeric state; notes MazG-like label is structural not functional. Noncentral imprecision: describes d1y6xa1 (1y6x A:7-93) as a 'domain fragment' compared with a 'full-domain record', although a trimmed residue range is a complete SCOPe domain, not a fragment annotation.

Correctly places c.55.1.1, c.55.1.3, c.55.1.4 in superfamily c.55.1 (fold c.55 Ribonuclease H-like, class c), all supported by the children/parents bundle. States remote common ancestry and shared structural/mechanistic core, and explicitly rejects shared substrate, chemistry, biological role, function transfer, and fold-only homology. Template remark is hedged as a hypothesis. All must_include/must_avoid met. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Families and sunids, superfamily a.25.1, fold a.25, class a all supported by children/parents calls. Correctly frames the three as remote homologs at superfamily level with family-level functional divergence, rejects fold-alone homology and function transfer, and notes other a.25.1 families so superfamily membership predicts no particular chemistry. Does not state what family-specific sequence, structure or experimental evidence is needed for metal/reaction/assembly/role claims.

Correct family/superfamily/fold placements with supported sunids and example domains (d1ikop_, d5n0ya1); frames the relationship as distant superfamily-level ancestry and refuses copper/electron-transfer transfer. Does not retrieve or use the family comments ('lacking the metal-binding site') and does not name conserved metal-ligand geometry as a required evidence type, pointing only to literature/UniProt/PDB annotations. No material errors. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Fold d.15, superfamily d.15.1, three families with sunids and Pfam supported; superfamily treated as a common-ancestry claim distinct from biochemical activity; rejects conjugation, Ras (and Rho) binding, and p97/VCP transfers, labelling p97 as non-SCOPe knowledge; names required external evidence. One loose phrase ('superfamily is a fold-level grouping') but the hierarchy is otherwise handled correctly. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22. Families c.23.1.1/c.23.1.4/c.23.1.5 verified as children of superfamily c.23.1, fold c.23, class c; superfamily correctly read as the level implying distant common origin, no family-level homology. Rejects phosphorelay/receiver function, ODC-wing catalysis (c.67.1.5, d.125.1.1 separate), circadian/KaiC mechanism, and antizyme regulation. Correctly notes KaiA C-terminal d1r8ja1 is a.186.1.1 (different fold) and that d1r8ja2's only annotation is a linker note. Acknowledges recruitment into multidomain proteins without using whole-protein function.

Correct b.84.5/b.84.5.1 placement and sibling superfamilies; fold as architecture only, superfamily as ancestry among family members, no ancestry asserted with b.84.1-b.84.4. Reasoning is thinner on hierarchy-as-hypothesis and does not note that withholding a homology claim is not a claim of non-relation. Factual slip: 1vdz is attributed to Thermus thermophilus, while the answer's own d1vdza2 lineage places it under Pyrococcus horikoshii; the 'complexed with mpd' comment is not in this bundle. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct fold f.21 (81344) and three superfamilies with sunids and f.21.2 family breakdown, all bundle-supported including fold core comment and the f.21.1/f.21.3 annotations. Treats fold as architectural grouping not ancestry, treats the 'possible link' note as a stated hypothesis not a merge, lists unsafe transfers, and says merger needs curated revision or independent sequence/structure evolutionary evidence. Does not overclaim non-homology. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct mapping of the three families to c.2.1.1/51736, c.2.1.8/51900, c.2.1.9/63944 under c.2.1 in fold c.2, class c, supported by bundle. Explicitly states that fold or class alone would not establish ancestry while superfamily placement does (remote homology); distinct families mean no close homology; function does not transfer; background functional statements flagged as unverified; family-level matching required for predictions. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Accurate same-family placement and lineage with solid designed-protein and function-transfer caveats. Claims the family placement is 'the only homology statement for the pair' while never checking the family node, so the 'not a true family' annotation on SUNID 100905 is absent. Decisive annotation ignored; bio capped at 2, factual 2. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct: 1.69 d1t1ja_ c.137.1.1 in one-member fold c.137 vs d1f8ya_ c.23.14.1, shared only at class level; 2.08 d1t1ja1 c.23.14.2 in superfamily c.23.14 as a new family beside c.23.14.1. Frames the move as SCOPe homology at superfamily level, family-level not claimed, distinguishes the superfamily label change from reclassification, and rejects function transfer. Correct SID change d1t1ja_ to d1t1ja1. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Full artifact lineage, annotation comment, and artifact_not_homology_evidence warning supported by bundle; d1a14h1 H:9-111 b.1.1.1 (Ig-like, Ig superfamily, V set, VH, mouse) correctly identified. Rejects using tag matches for fold/superfamily/family assignment; limits stated (tag origin inferred from classification, not sequence). Complete.

Correct 1.75 whole-chain f.11.1.1 and 2.08 split to b.179.1.1/f.60.1.1 with boundaries; good module inference, per-segment search guidance, and correct use of the in-bundle 3tewA record as sequence similarity only. States it did not check intermediate releases, so the 2.04 split release is omitted.

Identifiers, boundaries and SCCS all correct; mosaic and new fold d.394 for d3jb9a5 correct. But confuses hierarchy semantics: calls the bromodomain family placement (a.29.2.1) the 'weakest' link because it is short and says it 'should not be read as demonstrated bromodomain homology', inverting SCOPe meaning where family placement is the closest homology assertion; describes the other links at fold level rather than superfamily. Family-vs-superfamily confusion caps reasoning. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Cites the 're' flag and representative repeat correctly, but frames length variation as a whole-protein phenomenon via the mistaken claim that 'SCOPe classifies one repeat unit per domain'. The classified domains themselves (51, 373, 752 residues) span different numbers of repeats, so this confuses the complete multi-repeat domain with a single repeat unit, undermining the core answer. Honest that lengths and the species-level sccs resolution limit the evidence.

Correct metadata supported by bundle; cites 2.08 / 2.08-stable pinned with release=2.08, cites the dated periodic identifier alongside when exact reproducibility matters, and says the periodic label is not a new numbered release. Omits the content semantics of periodic updates (newly classified PDB entries added without rewriting stable-release domains). Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correctly reports a.47.2.1 (STAT-like, t-SNARE) for 1br0 A, 1ez3 A/B/C and 1dn1 B, the fragment comment and 'ms' flag, 1dn1 B's automated-matches parent and 'automated match to d3c98b_', d3c98b_ without flags, and 1dn1 obsolescence; all consistent with the bundle. Correctly reads fragment placement as applying to the three-helical region only, warns against inferring complete architecture, and limits function transfer. Does not explicitly make the point that the complete domain resolves the fragment-driven spectrin-like resemblance. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. States divergence within c.2.1 and treats cross-fold convergence as a hypothesis ('not something a fold difference proves', 'analogy or unresolved'), lists chemical constraint, chance motifs, catalytic convergence, and rejects function transfer; names curated placement plus structural topology/alignment statistics and profile/HMM as needed. Family listings for c.2.1 and c.3.1 and fold/superfamily sunids all verified. 'Should be treated as convergent or analogous unless...' is a default stance but is explicitly caveated. Minor unverifiable procedural notes (species-record lookup) are not material.

Correct 2.04 b.23.2.1 (fold b.23, SF b.23.2) to 2.08 b.18.1.36 superfamily b.18.1, same superfamily as Cry b.18.1.3 but different families, remote homology, l.1.1.1 tag noted, no function transfer. Avoids all must_avoid items.

Complete: family placement supports homology and survives the hf flag; hf defined correctly and scoped to d1ztra1 only; coordinates, alignments and residue mappings not transferable; mutant and nhe-complex comments considered; function not transferred; label-noise argument for fold-level training and same-group splits for family labels; hf domains flagged or excluded; limits stated. All release, lineage, comment and homology facts match the bundle. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22. Reasoning complete: homology retained at family level; fr semantics correct (domain scope, not inherited); alignment over covered region with coverage reported relative to family core and low scores not read as evidence against membership; d1uc6a1 preferred as non-fragment representative with d1o5dt2 kept as partial-coverage member; diversity counted at protein level but fragment not weighted equally; cr9 comment not transferred; limits stated. Factual support is sound but omits the domain residue boundaries (A:6-109, T:107-205) and domain sunids, which are material for a fragment-coverage question; no quality fields considered.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Confused opening ('assign it to a new fold ... only if') and a wrong final conclusion: argues a new superfamily 'would overstate the evidence' and recommends a fold-only provisional member, which SCOPe hierarchy does not allow and which contradicts must_include 1. Misstates superfamily semantics as 'common evolutionary origin with other members of the fold'. Level definitions and convergence caveat otherwise reasonable. Release facts asserted with empty bundle.

Correct hierarchy: d.144.1.7, d.144.1.6, d.144.1.4 as families of d.144.1 in fold d.144, class alpha+beta, release 2.08, with sibling families matching the children response. Correctly states superfamily grouping implies homology whereas fold sharing alone would be analogy; shared bilobal ATP-binding core with Mg-coordinating Asp; acceptor specificity set by family-specific loops and insertions. Rejects substrate and regulation transfer; requires activity assays, substrate-bound structures, mutagenesis, within-family motif alignment, and domain/partner data for regulation. Factual deduction: the APH member names and the claim that 'the name search for PI3K returned no hits' are not backed by any response in the bundle (only sccs, parents and children were retrieved); the member names are correct in SCOPe, but the search claim is an unsupported API-dependent statement. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-22.
